title: Phishing Triage, Malicious Link, and Attachment Response Playbook
source: CISA Phishing Defense Guidance & NIST SP 800-177 (Trustworthy Email)
content:
### 1. OVERVIEW & DETECTION
Phishing attacks deliver deceptive electronic communications containing malicious attachments (macros, ISO/IMG files, LNK shortcuts, PDF scripts, HTML smuggling) or deceptive hyperlinks pointing to credential harvesting landing pages or malware payloads. Detection indicators include:
- User-reported suspicious email submissions via phish alarm / reporting plugins.
- Email gateway (SEG) alerts flagging SPF, DKIM, or DMARC authentication failures (Authentication-Results: spf=fail, dkim=fail, dmarc=fail).
- High-risk attachment types detected in inbound email (e.g., .iso, .vhd, .lnk, .js, .hta, .html, .xlsm, password-protected archives).
- Inbound emails from newly registered lookalike / typosquatted domains impersonating internal executives, vendors, or common SaaS providers (e.g., Microsoft 365, DocuSign, Google Workspace).
- URL rewrite telemetry indicating users clicked on links later categorized as malicious.

### 2. EVIDENCE & ARTIFACTS TO EXAMINE
- Raw Email Headers (.eml / .msg): Inspect Return-Path, From, Reply-To, Received headers (to trace true originating mail server IP), Message-ID, and Authentication-Results.
- Attachment Hashes & Sandbox Detonation: Extract SHA-256 hashes of attached files and detonated attachments in sandbox environments to inspect spawned processes, child threads, and network callbacks.
- Link Destinations: Unshorten and detonate embedded URLs; inspect redirect chains, landing page HTML, and credential submission endpoints.
- Web Proxy & EDR Telemetry: Correlate user clicks with corporate web proxy logs and endpoint process events (e.g., Outlook spawning browser or office application spawning cmd.exe or powershell.exe).

### 3. INVESTIGATION & TRIAGE
- Blast Radius Determination: Query email server logs (Exchange Online / Google Workspace Message Trace) by Subject line, Sender address, and Sender IP to identify all recipients within the organization who received the same email campaign.
- User Interaction Assessment: Determine whether recipients merely received, opened, clicked links, or submitted credentials / executed attachments.
- Authentication Log Check: If credential phishing is suspected, inspect Microsoft Entra ID / Okta logs for successful logins from unusual IP addresses, unfamiliar user agents, or impossible travel immediately following the email timestamp.

### 4. CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES
- Tenant-Wide Email Purge: Use administrative compliance tools (e.g., Microsoft Defender for Office 365 / PowerShell Search-Mailbox or Google Vault) to hard-delete the phishing email across all enterprise mailboxes.
- Domain & URL Block: Add malicious sender domains, sender IPs, and destination URLs to the Secure Email Gateway, web proxy, and perimeter firewall blocklists.
- Credential Reset & Session Revocation: Immediately force password reset and revoke all active OAuth / refresh tokens and browser sessions for any user who clicked or entered credentials.

### 5. ERADICATION, RECOVERY & REMEDIATION
- Endpoint Remediation: If an attachment was opened, isolate the endpoint and perform full EDR investigation for persistence mechanisms, injected binaries, and scheduled tasks.
- Enforce Phishing-Resistant MFA: Deploy FIDO2 / WebAuthn hardware security keys or certificate-based authentication to neutralize credential phishing attacks.
- Configure Strict DMARC Policy: Enforce p=reject or p=quarantine for organizational email domains, along with strict SPF and DKIM signing.
- Security Awareness Feedback: Provide targeted, supportive feedback and training to affected users involved in the incident.
